title: M.A. / M.Sc in Your Subject (after ITEP)

value.body: The Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP) combines a bachelor's degree with a B.Ed in four years. To teach senior classes (as a PGT) or to move towards college teaching, many ITEP graduates take a master's — M.A., M.Sc or M.Com — in their subject. Planning the subject early helps, because master's admission usually depends on what you studied as your main subject.

items.label: ITEP length
items.note: B.A. B.Ed / B.Sc. B.Ed / B.Com. B.Ed, under NCTE

items.label: Master's length
items.note: Some universities allow a one-year master's after a four-year degree; check eligibility

items.label: PGT requirement
items.note: As per common recruitment rules, e.g. KVS and NVS

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Admission to a subject master's is through CUET-PG (central and many state universities), university entrance tests or merit. Your ITEP major subject usually needs to match the master's subject. For college teaching, you then need UGC-NET (or a state eligibility test) or a PhD.

value.title: At a glance
items: The B.Ed component of ITEP already counts, so a master's is what PGT eligibility adds.
Whether a university accepts ITEP for a one-year master's varies — confirm before applying.
Teacher recruitment exams (state TETs, CTET for lower classes, PGT exams) run alongside.
A master's plus NET also opens research and JRF routes.
